title: An early-exit reader on a pipe inside a pipefail shell script fails the pipeline whenever its writer still has a write to make, so the script ends or takes the wrong branch: 35 sites, one of which reddened CI after the 3.2.5 cut
body:
Found by dc on 2026-10-23, from the CI red that hv raised after the 3.2.5 cut. vc confirmed the diagnosis the same morning.

## What reddened CI

Two pushes after the cut failed "Intent Tests" on the Ubuntu leg, step "Run tests": run 39857791246 (bbd91e70f) and run 39859110923 (bea253129), both on 2026-10-22. Both failed one arm, `canon: a clean estate exits 0` (`tests/unit/devbin_canon.bats:37`), whose only output was `comm: write error: Broken pipe`. The release commit 2e0e9215d passed the same arm an hour earlier. The macOS leg is skipped on a push.

`bin/.devbin/cmd/canon:177` ran `first_both="$(comm -12 <(…) <(…) | head -1)"` under `set -euo pipefail`. comm's output was about 6 KB, so GNU comm flushed a 4 KiB stdio buffer and then wrote the rest at exit. When `head -1` had already printed its line and exited, that second write got EPIPE. GitHub's runners start steps with SIGPIPE ignored, so comm printed the error and exited 1 rather than dying of the signal. pipefail failed the substitution and `set -e` ended the script. Scheduling decided whether it fired, which is why the tag passed and the next two pushes did not.

Made deterministic, with comm writing 84500 bytes (`refs/bank/dc/canon-pipe/canon-race.sh`, log `canon-race.log`): the base canon exits 141 with SIGPIPE at default, so macOS fails too once the output outruns the pipe, and exits 1 with `comm: stdout: Broken pipe` with SIGPIPE ignored. The fixed canon exits 0 both ways. canon's own fix is `refs/bank/dc/canon-pipe/fix`, banked on its own.

## The class

An early-exit reader on a pipe (`| head`, `| grep -q`, `| sed -n Nq`, `| awk '{…; exit}'`), inside a script that sets pipefail, fails the pipeline whenever its writer still has a write to make after the reader exits. With SIGPIPE at default the writer dies with 141; with it ignored the writer gets EPIPE and usually exits 1. Either way pipefail reports the pipeline as failed. What that does depends on where the pipeline sits:

- **As a statement, or as the right side of an assignment, under `set -e`:** the script ends.
- **As an `if`, `elif` or `&&` condition:** it silently takes the other branch. A match that `grep -q` found reads as no match.
- **Behind `|| true`:** harmless.

It is the shell twin of issue 0613, where a Rust verb whose reader stopped reading panicked with exit 101.

## Where, at 0e0f340d6 (35 sites, measured)

Census: every tracked file under `bin`, `lib/templates`, `tests` and `intent/plugins` with a bash or sh shebang (or a `shellcheck shell=` directive) that sets pipefail, then every non-comment line piping into `head`, `grep -q…`, `sed -n Nq` or an `awk` program that exits.

- `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos` (10): 175, 642, 671, 706, 708, 1341, 1342, 2037, 2199, 2205. Lines 708 and 2205 are `xcrun notarytool … | head -40` in the release path, so a long notarisation log ends `publish`. Line 671 is a condition.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/measured` (4): 176 (condition), 278, 532 and 542 (`printf | head -N | while`, statements).
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/linux` (4): 84, 202 and 212 (conditions), 138.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/hosting` (3): 144 and 146 (conditions), 154.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/vendor` (2): 115, 116.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/local` (2): 441, 502.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/prepush` (1): 346, `printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED" | grep -qE '^(native/|…)'` inside `if !`. A push range large enough to outrun the pipe can read a native change as none.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/suite` (1): 127, `grep -E '^not ok ' "$out" | head -20`, a statement. A run with many reds ends the suite command after it prints them.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/canon` (1): 177, the CI red above, fixed by `refs/bank/dc/canon-pipe/fix`.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/hooks` (1): 169.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/cache` (1): 131, inside another command's arguments, so its status is not read.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/precommit` (1): 226, behind `|| true`.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/brew` (1): 329, behind `|| true`.
- `intent/plugins/claude/skills/in-cost-analysis/scripts/cost-metrics.sh` (1): 331, `git log --reverse … | head -1` in an assignment. On a long history the script ends.
- `intent/plugins/claude/skills/in-tca-finish/scripts/tca-report.sh` (2): 170 and 242, behind `|| true`.

Not measured: whether each writer can outrun the pipe in use. Most writers here are small today, which is how canon's was until it was not. The census is a regex, so a site it does not match, such as a reader on a later line of a multi-line pipeline, is not in this list.

## Expected

No early-exit reader sits on a pipe in a pipefail script where its failure can end the script or turn a branch. Each site either reads all of its input (`sed -n 1p`, `awk 'NR == 1'`), takes the first line by parameter expansion from a value already held, or reads a here-string or a file instead of a pipe. A site behind `|| true` is left as it is and says why. A shell rule in the critic with a greppable detection then keeps the class out of new code, so the commit gate refuses it rather than a CI runner finding it.

## Spec (vc, 2026-10-23, under hv's go; hv's words on this class, verbatim: "I don't want this shite to keep happening")

LANE: dc, one bank, banked ahead of this spec at refs/bank/dc/0628/fix (blob 24053b9c0f5e, patch-id bc11c2b90db7) and judged against it. SHAPE: every early-exit reader on a real pipe inside a pipefail script is replaced by a form that reads all of its input or reads none through a pipe: a condition over a value becomes `grep -q ... <<<"$x"`; a first-line assignment becomes a capture plus `${v%%$'\n'*}`; a first-N print becomes `sed -n '1,Np'`; an awk early exit becomes a flag and an END block. Sites behind `|| true` are left and listed, since their failure is already discarded, and canon:177 lands in its own bank (refs/bank/dc/canon-pipe/fix). The census list is part of this record. PROOF: the mechanism's deterministic control is canon-pipe's, a writer whose output outruns the pipe, run with SIGPIPE at default and ignored (base rc 141 and rc 1 with `comm: stdout: Broken pipe`; fix rc 0 both ways); for the class bank, the whole bats suite on the base and on the fix, red sets diffed by name both ways, a census over the fixed tree that finds only the sites left on purpose, and `intent critic shell` clean with shellcheck armed. cost-metrics.sh ships in the support tree, so the bank carries a CHANGELOG Fixed line under `## [3.2.6] - in progress`. CLOSES WHEN: the bank lands and `intent issues close 0628` names the sha; the kovacs preflight's first run on that HEAD is the live confirmation. THE PREFLIGHT ITSELF (hv's ruling in the TUI, 2026-10-23): a standing kovacs order, banked and sha256-checked like ORDER 8 (refs/bank/dc/preflight/preflight-linux.sh), runs tests.yml's Ubuntu leg exactly under `trap '' PIPE` on a fresh clone at the candidate sha and copies its summary back to this Mac; the pre-push hook REFUSES a push to upstream whose HEAD has no green summary, a push to local needs none, and releasing.md carries the step.

## Judged (dc, 2026-10-23)

THE WHOLE BATS SUITE, BASE AGAINST FIX. Base `tmp/wt-dc-0628base` at 95cafd2ac (tree 56af7460a5bd) against fix `tmp/wt-dc-0628fix`, the bank plus its CHANGELOG line (tree dd0d1d24b364), run one after the other from 14:50:59Z to 14:57:35Z by date -u, both against the installed pair at 2e0e9215d with SIGPIPE at its default (`refs/bank/dc/0628/judge-0628.sh`, blob 29915ce40941; summary `evidence/run1-summary.txt`, 459c6a8b9e27). The base ran 783 ok and 11 not ok, and the fix the same. Red only on the base: none. Red only on the fix: none. Red on both: the same eleven `intent claude rules validate` arms (`evidence/base.red` and `evidence/fix.red` are one blob, e44b7927533f). They are an artefact of the judging setup: a worktree's rule file validated by the main tree's pair, whose library holds the same id, reads as a duplicate id. `tests/unit/rule_pack_shell.bats` is green on main against the same pair.

THE CENSUS OVER THE FIXED TREE, the command this record's census used, run in the fix tree (`evidence/census-fixed.txt`, 4a7ab002d8e9): four sites, the four left on purpose behind `|| true` (brew:329, precommit:226, tca-report.sh:170 and 242). canon:177 landed on its own at 04705176a.

THE CRITIC. `intent critic shell` over the eleven changed files at every severity is clean, with IN-SH-CODE-001 and IN-SH-CODE-002 both armed by shellcheck 0.11.0 and both run (`evidence/critic-shell-fix.log`, ce53dabc5d84). The base reads the same.

THE BANK FOR LANDING: `refs/bank/dc/0628/fix-b` (blob 00e64198872b, patch-id 5407ab3fb3f1), the judged bank rebased onto 4d10120ed with its CHANGELOG line under `## [3.2.6] - in progress`, `### Fixed`, below the `### Added` that cc's 3c2ed2d39 put above it. Its code hunks carry the judged bank's patch-id, bc11c2b90db7, and its CHANGELOG line is byte-identical to the judged tree's.

A CORRECTION, MEASURED. The census above says of cost-metrics.sh:331 "On a long history the script ends". It does not. On this repository's 8,612 commits, `git log --reverse ... | head -1` does fail, rc 141, but the line sits in `collect_git_history`, which the script calls only as `GIT_JSON="$(collect_git_history)"`, and errexit is off inside a command substitution unless `inherit_errexit` is set, which the script does not set. So the script carries on with the right first date. A reduction of the script's shape (`evidence/cm-probe.sh`, 3ff6b75236fd) reached the step after every time, under /bin/bash 3.2.57 and bash 5.3.20, with SIGPIPE at its default and ignored. The fix stays, because it is the class's shape and would end the script the day the function is called any other way. The CHANGELOG line says that no output changes today, and vc ruled that it stays. The census's other "ends the script" readings are source reads that did not check whether errexit is off where the line runs.
